content.text:
1. `createCommentAction` in [create-comment.ts](src/actions/comments/create-comment.ts) validates and authorizes the request, applies a rate limit, then calls `createComment` in [comment-service.ts](src/server/services/comment-service.ts).

2. `createComment` calls `resolveMentionedUsers`, which loads up to 100 organization members through `memberRepo.listMembers`. In [mentions.ts](src/lib/mentions.ts), `extractMentions` finds distinct `@handles` in the body, ignoring code spans and fenced blocks. `handleOf` defines a member’s handle as the lowercased part of their email before `@`, and `resolveMentions` maps matching handles to `userId`s. Unknown handles are dropped. The service also keeps client-provided IDs if they belong to one of those loaded members, then deduplicates both lists.

3. The resolved IDs are written onto the comment as JSON by `commentRepo.insertComment` in [comment-repository.ts](src/server/repositories/comment-repository.ts); the `mentionedUserIds` field is defined in [comments.ts](src/server/db/schema/comments.ts). The service then emits `comment.created` with the same IDs. That event payload carries the list forward; the notification fan-out does not parse the body again.

4. `notification-service.ts` subscribes to `comment.created` when the module loads. [event-registry.ts](src/server/services/event-registry.ts) imports it, and `src/instrumentation.ts` registers the event handlers at process startup. The subscriber calls `notify` for the issue’s author and assignee as comment watchers, then calls `notify` with kind `comment_mention` for the mentioned IDs.

5. `notify` deduplicates recipients and skips the actor, then reads each recipient’s preference for that notification kind via `preferenceRepo.getPreference`. `resolveChannels` decides the channels: with no saved preference, the default is both `in_app` and `email`; with a preference, `inApp` controls the in-app channel and `email` controls email. If `digestOnly` is set, immediate email is allowed only when the organization’s `digest_email` feature flag is enabled; the in-app channel still follows `inApp`. If no channels remain, `notify` skips that recipient entirely.

6. For recipients with at least one channel, `notificationRepo.insertNotifications` stores a row with the chosen channels, `recipientId`, kind, and content. That row is what appears in the in-app inbox when it includes `in_app`. An `email` channel records email eligibility on the notification; it does not send an immediate mention email in this path. Digest processing in [digest-service.ts](src/server/services/digest-service.ts) and [digest-email-job.ts](src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts) later builds and sends a digest from unread notifications for digest subscribers. `sendEmail` in [email-service.ts](src/server/services/email-service.ts) currently logs the rendered draft.

So the mention recipient can get both channels, an in-app row only, email eligibility only, or no row if they are the actor or all channels are disabled. Unknown handles never reach this decision because they do not resolve to user IDs.
